sources.title: MSL Mars Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) Reduced Data Record V1.0
variablesUsed: QC (8-bit quality control string; required QC=='00000000')
sources.role: Primary surface ionizing radiation reference (Gale Crater, Mars).

sources.title: MAVEN Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) Instrument Package
sources.role: Orbital energetic particle context for the September 2017 SEP event (Lee et al., 2018; Zeitlin et al., 2018). Not converted directly to surface dose without atmospheric transport.

sources.title: Mars 2020 Jezero Crater Digital Elevation Model (DEM)
sources.role: 16-azimuth local topographic horizon obstruction and sky-visibility solid-angle fraction (Terrain Shielding Potential — Experimental).

sources.title: Peer-Reviewed Mars Surface Dosimetry Benchmarks
citations: Hassler, D. M., et al. (2014), Mars' Surface Radiation Environment Measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity Rover, Science, 343(6169), 1244797.
Zeitlin, C., et al. (2018), Analysis of the Radiation Hazard Observed by RAD on the Surface of Mars During the September 2017 Solar Particle Event, Geophys. Res. Lett., 45, 5845–5851.
Guo, J., et al. (2021), Radiation environment for future human exploration on the surface of Mars, Astron. Astrophys. Rev., 29, 8.

processingSteps: 1. Connected to NASA PDS PPI archive (MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0) and parsed detached PDS3 .LBL byte pointers for observation headers and DOSIMETRY sections.
2. Filtered observations by quality control flag QC == '00000000', observation duration >= 120 s, and finite positive detector B & E dose rates.
3. Preserved physical units (microGray/hour for absorbed dose rate; microGray for integrated absorbed dose) without conflating Gray (Gy) and Sievert (Sv).
4. Computed 16-azimuth ray-marched horizon elevation angles and upper-hemisphere sky visibility fraction (Omega_sky / 2pi) across the 256x256 Jezero DEM grid.
5. Separated the regional Radiation Exposure reference layer from the experimental Terrain Shielding Potential layer.
